title: MFA enforcement and session revocation
summary: Identity provider enforces multi-factor authentication on the principal and supports administrator-initiated revocation of all live sessions, refresh tokens, and persistent device grants. The control couples preventive MFA hardening (D3-MFA) with reactive session-revocation capability so an operator can both raise the bar and evict an active attacker.

component.title: Identity provider — MFA + session revocation profile
component.description: IdP configuration that enforces phishing-resistant MFA for the principal and exposes an admin API for blanket session revocation across IdP-issued tokens and downstream SaaS sessions.

control-implementations.description: Implements identification, authentication, and account-management requirements via enforced MFA and administrator session control.

implemented-requirements.description: Identification and authentication (organisational users) — phishing-resistant MFA required for the principal across IdP and downstream SaaS.
Authenticator management — MFA factor enrolment, rotation, and revocation are administered through the IdP.
Account management — administrator can revoke all live sessions and refresh tokens for the principal.
Unsuccessful logon attempts — IdP enforces lockout / risk-based step-up on repeated failures, including password-spray patterns.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — IA-2, IA-5, AC-2, AC-7
